planting.note: Set divisions or potted plants in spring into lean, well-drained, calcareous clay or loam in full sun to light shade.

directions: Tradescantia hirsutiflora is a clump-forming perennial native to calcareous prairies, open woods, and limestone glades across the south-central United States, including the Texas Blackland Prairie, where upright, slightly pubescent stems and narrow grass-like leaves emerge in early spring. From March into summer it produces small, three-petaled violet to blue-purple flowers in loose terminal clusters, each bloom lasting only a morning before closing by midday. Plant in well-drained, alkaline to neutral clay or loam in full sun to light shade; established clumps tolerate drought and summer heat with little care. Divide crowded clumps in early spring or fall to maintain vigor and control spread.

planting.note: Direct sow or set out transplants in early spring into lean, alkaline, sharply drained soil in full sun.

directions: Stenaria nigricans, commonly called diamond flowers or prairie bluet, is a low, woody-based perennial of calcareous prairies, limestone glades, and rocky open ground across the central and southern United States, including the Texas Blackland Prairie. Its wiry, branching stems carry narrow needle-like leaves and are studded from late spring through fall with tiny white to pale-pink, four-lobed tubular flowers that draw small native bees and butterflies. It thrives in lean, alkaline, well-drained soil and full sun, tolerating heat, drought, and poor rocky ground once established, making it a durable edging or rock-garden plant. Direct sow in fall or early spring and avoid rich, moist soils, which encourage floppy growth and reduce flowering.
